answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to earn a small, time-locked stake before its actions count toward reputation. The stake is returned as the agent completes independently verified tasks; failed or duplicate work is slashed. A signal from one account is then weighted by its earned history, while an echo of the same claim across fresh accounts adds little. A prism of task types and independent reviewers makes copying harder. Sybils remain possible, but the attacker must tie up capital and repeat costly work for each identity.
